target_customer: Drug and medical device sponsors that run clinical trials
problem: Clinical trials rely on legacy EDC software and large CRO teams. Harbor sells an AI-native EDC and is expanding into full-service trial execution built on that system of record.
business_model: EDC software contracts plus full-service CRO contracts (company states a $1.93M three year CRO contract)
product_category: AI-native EDC and contract research organization

founders.name: Albert Cai
prior_employers: Biolinq (clinical trials and regulatory strategy; took first product to FDA De Novo)
education: Oklahoma School of Science and Mathematics
founders.background_notes: YC launch post says he spent two years as a medical device industry analyst.

founders.name: Nathan H. Leung
prior_employers: Employee 1 at a previous YC startup

competitors.what: Incumbent EDC; Study Builder Agent configures EDC forms and visits for existing customers
competitors.traction_then: Large installed base; AI agent announced 2026

competitors.name: Evinova
competitors.what: AI-native clinical platform expanding with pharma partners
competitors.traction_then: Partnerships with Astellas, AstraZeneca and Bristol Myers Squibb in February 2026

competitors.name: Clinion
competitors.what: EDC marketed as AI-native with configurable builds and real-time edit checks

technical_complexity.rationale: EDC needs 21 CFR Part 11, GCP and HIPAA compliance plus protocol-to-build automation. Hard parts are regulated validation and reliability rather than novel research.

defensibility.rationale: Trial data systems are sticky once a study is running, and owning the system of record lets Harbor expand into services. Incumbents and AI-native rivals are numerous.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents added AI features in 2026 (Veeva Study Builder Agent; Medidata Plus announced 2026-07-23, after the batch started). Outcome for Harbor unknown.

market_need_then: Company cites clinical trials as 45% of new drug and device development spend and an $82B CRO market. Its own early traction: seven trials and about $15.6k monthly software revenue per the YC launch post.

branding.domain_note: Uses runharbor.com, a prefix variant of harbor.com.

identity.logo: Logo file exists on YC data; design not viewed
identity.voice_and_tone: The intelligent EDC; speed and automation versus legacy; Magic Build, Magic Capture, Magic Monitor feature names

branding.community_and_virality: Covered in a March 2026 magazine feature and a YC launch post offering a setup-fee waiver for Launch YC mentions.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic dictionary name shared with several unrelated Harbor products (an open-source agent framework, a local LLM CLI, an insurance startup), so search and recall are weak.

pivots.from: AI system of record for clinical trial data (EDC)
pivots.to: Full-service AI-native CRO built on the EDC
pivots.why: Services are the largest spend line; owning the system of record lets Harbor deliver them (company statement; exact date not given)

outcome_analysis: Harbor is an active Spring 2026 company with early revenue it states at $187k contracted software revenue and a $1.93M three year CRO contract, both company-reported. The CEO's clinical and FDA background and a CTO from Google and Ramp fit the problem. Risks include incumbents' AI features, long regulated sales cycles and the shift from software to a services business.
notes: Funding: VCBacked and FundedIQ list a $500K pre-seed in June 2026 with Y Combinator and Neuronfeed lists a $500K seed in January 2026; all aggregators, standard YC deal, conflicting dates, so unverified and not recorded as rounds. Revenue figures are company-stated only. Location conflict: San Francisco (YC) versus San Diego (company site). Nathan's role as employee 1 at a YC startup is unnamed. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition news. Completeness pass: the 500K pre-seed rests on databases only (VCBacked and FundedIQ say 2026-06; Neuronfeed says a seed in 2026-01), likely the standard YC deal. Date conflict unresolved. Press search found no coverage.
